accepted.s: The National Investment Fund (NIF) was set up on which date?
accepted.x: The National Investment Fund was set up on 3 November 2005.
accepted.tq: Use the precise date to distinguish the fund from later disinvestment institutions.
accepted.sec: Disinvestment proceeds - National Investment Fund, Budget targets, strategic sale  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the use of proceeds credited to the National Investment Fund?
o: Only the income generated from the fund is used.
The entire principal is distributed annually to CPSE employees.
The proceeds are transferred exclusively to State governments.
The fund is used only for purchasing foreign exchange.
accepted.x: The proceeds are credited to the National Investment Fund, but only the income generated from it is used.
accepted.tq: Test the distinction between principal proceeds and income generated from a fund.
accepted.sec: Disinvestment proceeds - National Investment Fund, Budget targets, strategic sale  [other exams]

accepted.s:
With reference to disinvestment targets, consider the following statements:
1. The target for 2020–21 from PSBs and financial institutions was ₹90,000 crore.
2. The target for 2025–26 was ₹47,000 crore.
3. The target for 2026–27 was ₹80,000 crore.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: the respective targets were ₹90,000 crore, ₹47,000 crore and ₹80,000 crore.
accepted.tq: Compare closely placed budget years and figures.
accepted.sec: Disinvestment proceeds - National Investment Fund, Budget targets, strategic sale  [other exams]

accepted.s: Since which financial year has there been no separate disinvestment head in the Budget, with disinvestment receipts merged into Miscellaneous Capital Receipts?
accepted.x: Since FY24, there has been no separate disinvestment head; it has been merged into Miscellaneous Capital Receipts.
accepted.tq: Use the time marker to identify the change in budget classification.
accepted.sec: Disinvestment proceeds - National Investment Fund, Budget targets, strategic sale  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding strategic disinvestment:
1. In-principle approval has been given since 2016 for strategic disinvestment of 36 CPSEs.
2. Of these, 13 strategic disinvestments had been completed.
3. Strategic disinvestment refers only to sale of minority shares through an exchange offer.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Strategic disinvestment is not limited to sale of minority shares through an exchange offer.
accepted.tq: Find the false definition hidden among numerical statements.
accepted.sec: Disinvestment proceeds - National Investment Fund, Budget targets, strategic sale  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Modern Food Industries was sold to Hindustan Lever. BALCO was sold to Sterlite, VSNL to the Tata group and Air India to Tata Group.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure buyer-company pair and eliminate swapped buyers.
accepted.sec: Disinvestment proceeds - National Investment Fund, Budget targets, strategic sale  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following strategic sales in chronological order:
A. Air India
B. VSNL
C. Modern Food Industries
D. BALCO
accepted.x: The correct order is Modern Food Industries (2000), BALCO (2001), VSNL (2002) and Air India (2021).
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then arrange the intervening years.
accepted.sec: Disinvestment proceeds - National Investment Fund, Budget targets, strategic sale  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Bharat Bond ETF raised approximately what amount in 2019?
accepted.x: The Bharat Bond ETF raised approximately ₹32,400 crore in 2019.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the ETF mobilisation figure from individual CPSE sale proceeds.
accepted.sec: Disinvestment proceeds - National Investment Fund, Budget targets, strategic sale  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the disinvestment outcome stated?
o: LIC IPO — conducted in 2019 with about 32 lakh applications
NINL — sale proceeds credited to the exchequer from government equity
REC — acquired by PFC for ₹14,500 crore
BPCL — strategic sale completed in mid-2022
accepted.x: REC was acquired by PFC for ₹14,500 crore in 2018–19. NINL yielded no proceeds to the exchequer because the government held no equity; the BPCL sale was called off and the LIC IPO was in 2022 with about 73 lakh applications.
accepted.tq: Check the company, transaction and outcome together rather than recognising only the company name.
accepted.sec: Disinvestment proceeds - National Investment Fund, Budget targets, strategic sale  [other exams]

accepted.s: The disinvestment target and realisation for 2021–22 were, respectively:
accepted.x: For 2021–22, the target was ₹1.75 lakh crore, whereas the realisation was only about ₹13,534 crore.
accepted.tq: Separate target figures from actual realisations in the same financial year.
accepted.sec: Disinvestment proceeds - National Investment Fund, Budget targets, strategic sale  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about disinvestment transactions is correct?
o: HPCL was sold to ONGC in 2017–18 for ₹36,915 crore.
Pawan Hans and Central Electronics sales were completed without delay.
The 2022–23 realisation of ₹35,294 crore came only from the LIC IPO.
IDBI Bank strategic sale was abandoned after completion.
accepted.x: HPCL was sold to ONGC in 2017–18 for ₹36,915 crore. The 2022–23 realisation involved several entities, while Pawan Hans and Central Electronics sales stalled and IDBI Bank remained in the pipeline.
accepted.tq: Use the buyer, year and amount as a three-part identification test.
accepted.sec: Disinvestment proceeds - National Investment Fund, Budget targets, strategic sale  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Industrial (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951 is primarily associated with:
accepted.x: The Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951 is associated with industrial licensing.
accepted.tq: Link each Act with its distinctive regulatory purpose.
accepted.sec: Chronology of economic regulation Acts - IDRA, MRTP, FERA, FEMA, Competition Act  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: The Competition Act was enacted in 2002 and commenced on 31 March 2003. The other pairs are correctly matched.
accepted.tq: Find the wrong year among a set of familiar regulatory enactments.
accepted.sec: Chronology of economic regulation Acts - IDRA, MRTP, FERA, FEMA, Competition Act  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which Act was replaced by the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 in relation to the earlier sick-industrial-company regime?
accepted.x: The IBC, 2016 replaced the SICA regime, which had been associated with the functioning of BIFR.
accepted.tq: Identify the predecessor regime rather than the more widely known foreign-exchange replacement.
accepted.sec: Chronology of economic regulation Acts - IDRA, MRTP, FERA, FEMA, Competition Act  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following is the correct chronological order of the enactment of FEMA, the Competition Act and the IBC?
accepted.x: FEMA was enacted in 1999, the Competition Act in 2002 and the IBC in 2016.
accepted.tq: Arrange the Acts by their enactment years, not their commencement dates.
accepted.sec: Chronology of economic regulation Acts - IDRA, MRTP, FERA, FEMA, Competition Act  [other exams]

accepted.s: The National Renewal Fund, established in 1992, was intended primarily to provide:
o: A safety net and voluntary retirement support for workers affected by restructuring
Foreign exchange support to export-oriented industries
Direct loans to State electricity regulators
accepted.x: The National Renewal Fund provided a safety net, including VRS support, for workers affected by industrial restructuring.
accepted.tq: Match the fund with its beneficiary and policy purpose.
accepted.sec: PSE restructuring - NRF, BIFR, IBC, NCLT, New PSE Policy 2021  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about BIFR:
1. It was created under SICA, 1985.
2. It began functioning in 1987.
3. It was dissolved on 1 December 2016.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. BIFR was created under SICA, began functioning in 1987 and was dissolved on 1 December 2016.
accepted.tq: Test an institutional timeline through three linked dates.
accepted.sec: PSE restructuring - NRF, BIFR, IBC, NCLT, New PSE Policy 2021  [other exams]

accepted.s: After the dissolution of BIFR, its cases were transferred to which institutions under the IBC framework?
accepted.x: Following BIFR's dissolution, cases were transferred to the NCLT and NCLAT under the IBC framework.
accepted.tq: Trace the institutional successor relationship after a statutory body is dissolved.
accepted.sec: PSE restructuring - NRF, BIFR, IBC, NCLT, New PSE Policy 2021  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016?
o: It provides a time-bound, creditor-in-control resolution process.
It restores the earlier debtor-in-control SICA process.
It regulates only foreign exchange transactions.
It abolished the NCLT appellate structure.
accepted.x: The IBC provides a time-bound resolution process based on creditor control. Its regulator is the IBBI.
accepted.tq: Identify the core operational features of the law rather than its year alone.
accepted.sec: PSE restructuring - NRF, BIFR, IBC, NCLT, New PSE Policy 2021  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 was enacted on 28 May 2016 following the recommendations of which body?
o: T.K. Viswanathan-led Bankruptcy Law Reforms Committee
accepted.x: The IBC followed the recommendations of the T.K. Viswanathan-led Bankruptcy Law Reforms Committee, which reported in 2015.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between committees associated with insolvency, company law and competition policy.
accepted.sec: PSE restructuring - NRF, BIFR, IBC, NCLT, New PSE Policy 2021  [other exams]

accepted.s: The National Company Law Tribunal was established under which provision and from which date?
o: Section 410 of the Companies Act, 2013; 1 December 2016
Section 408 of the Companies Act, 2013; 1 June 2016
Section 5 of the Competition Act; 14 October 2003
accepted.x: The NCLT was established under Section 408 of the Companies Act, 2013, on 1 June 2016, following the Eradi Committee's recommendations.
accepted.tq: Combine the statutory section, establishing law and date in one precise recall question.
accepted.sec: PSE restructuring - NRF, BIFR, IBC, NCLT, New PSE Policy 2021  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which statement regarding NCLAT is correct?
o: It was created under Section 408 and hears only tax appeals.
It began functioning before the NCLT was established.
It replaced the CCI in investigating anti-competitive agreements.
It is constituted under Section 410 of the Companies Act, 2013 and has heard CCI appeals since 26 May 2017.
accepted.x: NCLAT is associated with Section 410 of the Companies Act, 2013 and has also heard appeals from CCI orders since 26 May 2017.
accepted.tq: Separate the roles and statutory sections of NCLT and NCLAT.
accepted.sec: PSE restructuring - NRF, BIFR, IBC, NCLT, New PSE Policy 2021  [other exams]

accepted.s: Under the New PSE Policy, 2021, which of the following is classified as a strategic sector?
accepted.x: Atomic energy, space and defence constitute one of the four strategic-sector groupings under the New PSE Policy, 2021.
accepted.tq: Recognise the official strategic-sector grouping rather than a general public-sector activity.
accepted.sec: PSE restructuring - NRF, BIFR, IBC, NCLT, New PSE Policy 2021  [other exams]

accepted.s: Under the New PSE Policy, 2021, the number of CPSEs to be retained in each strategic sector is intended to be:
o: Unlimited, depending on State government approval
Bare minimum, generally one to four
accepted.x: The policy envisages retaining a bare minimum of CPSEs, generally between one and four, in each strategic sector.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a range-based policy expression from an absolute numerical rule.
accepted.sec: PSE restructuring - NRF, BIFR, IBC, NCLT, New PSE Policy 2021  [other exams]

accepted.s: What is the stated policy approach towards CPSEs in non-strategic sectors under the New PSE Policy, 2021?
o: Mandatory expansion of all such CPSEs
accepted.x: CPSEs in non-strategic sectors are to be considered for privatisation, merger or closure.
accepted.tq: Use the policy's three-way action list to identify the correct option.
accepted.sec: PSE restructuring - NRF, BIFR, IBC, NCLT, New PSE Policy 2021  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: 16th Finance Commission — closure of 308 inactive State PSUs and privatisation of DISCOMs
IBBI — hearing appeals against CCI orders
BIFR — monetisation of surplus CPSE land
accepted.x: The 16th Finance Commission proposed closing 308 inactive State PSUs and privatising DISCOMs. The other institutions have different functions.
accepted.tq: Use institutional-function matching and reject authority swaps.
accepted.sec: PSE restructuring - NRF, BIFR, IBC, NCLT, New PSE Policy 2021  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Economic Survey 2025–26 proposal regarding listed CPSEs seeks to permit government shareholding to fall to:
o: 49%, while converting them into private companies
accepted.x: The proposal allows government stake in listed CPSEs to fall to 26% while retaining their Government company status.
accepted.tq: Test the percentage threshold together with its qualifying condition.
accepted.sec: PSE restructuring - NRF, BIFR, IBC, NCLT, New PSE Policy 2021  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Competition Act, 2002 was recommended by which committee?
accepted.x: The Competition Act, 2002 was recommended by the S.V.S. Raghavan Committee in 2000.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the committee associated with competition law from committees on insolvency and company law.
accepted.sec: Competition Act 2002 - committee, CCI powers, agreements, dominance, combinations

accepted.s: Who introduced the Competition Bill in Parliament?
accepted.x: The Competition Act was introduced by Arun Jaitley.
accepted.tq: Identify the political introducer separately from the recommending expert committee.
accepted.sec: Competition Act 2002 - committee, CCI powers, agreements, dominance, combinations

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Competition Commission of India:
1. It was established on 14 October 2003.
2. It consists of a Chairperson and two to six members.
3. It functions under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs.
4. The Competition Act has been amended in 2007, 2009 and 2023.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. The CCI was established on 14 October 2003, has a Chairperson and two to six members, functions under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, and the Act was amended in 2007, 2009 and 2023.
accepted.tq: Combine composition, administrative control and amendment dates in one institutional question.
accepted.sec: Competition Act 2002 - committee, CCI powers, agreements, dominance, combinations

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT covered under anti-competitive agreements under Section 3 of the Competition Act?
o: Issue of government bonds by the Reserve Bank of India
accepted.x: Section 3 covers anti-competitive agreements such as cartels, bid-rigging and price-fixing. Issue of government bonds by the RBI is not one of the listed examples.
accepted.tq: Find the unrelated activity among the specific forms of prohibited agreement.
accepted.sec: Competition Act 2002 - committee, CCI powers, agreements, dominance, combinations

accepted.s: Unfair pricing and denial of market access are examples associated with:
o: Abuse of dominant position under Section 4
accepted.x: Unfair pricing and denial of market access are forms of abuse of dominant position covered under Section 4.
accepted.tq: Separate the conduct-based categories of agreement, dominance and combination.
accepted.sec: Competition Act 2002 - committee, CCI powers, agreements, dominance, combinations

accepted.s: Under the Competition Act, combinations under Sections 5 and 6 primarily relate to:
o: Mergers and acquisitions above prescribed thresholds
accepted.x: Sections 5 and 6 concern combinations such as mergers and acquisitions that cross prescribed thresholds.
accepted.tq: Match the statutory section with the transaction category it regulates.
accepted.sec: Competition Act 2002 - committee, CCI powers, agreements, dominance, combinations

accepted.s: What is the consequence when the CCI does not decide a combination within the prescribed deadline?
o: The parties are required to seek approval from the Finance Commission.
The combination is automatically prohibited forever.
The combination is deemed to be approved.
The matter is transferred to BIFR.
accepted.x: A combination is deemed to have been approved if the CCI misses the prescribed decision deadline.
accepted.tq: Apply the statutory time-limit consequence to a transaction scenario.
accepted.sec: Competition Act 2002 - committee, CCI powers, agreements, dominance, combinations

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with the penalty imposed by the CCI?
accepted.x: The CCI imposed a ₹213.14 crore penalty on Meta/WhatsApp in 2024. Google was fined ₹1,337 crore in 2022.
accepted.tq: Pair the entity, year and penalty amount without swapping cases.
accepted.sec: Competition Act 2002 - committee, CCI powers, agreements, dominance, combinations

accepted.s: With reference to the Meta/WhatsApp case, which statement is correct?
o: NCLAT cancelled the penalty and upheld the five-year data-sharing ban.
NCLAT upheld the penalty but set aside the five-year data-sharing ban; an appeal is pending before the Supreme Court.
The Supreme Court has already finally dismissed all proceedings.
The case concerned only industrial licensing under the IDRA.
accepted.x: In 2025, NCLAT upheld the penalty but set aside the five-year data-sharing ban; the Supreme Court appeal remains pending.
accepted.tq: Track the appellate outcome and distinguish penalty from remedial restriction.
accepted.sec: Competition Act 2002 - committee, CCI powers, agreements, dominance, combinations

accepted.s: The CCI's Digital Markets Division is associated with the regulation of:
accepted.x: The CCI set up a Digital Markets Division to address competition issues arising in digital markets.
accepted.tq: Infer the institutional function directly from the specialised division's domain.
